answer: Mirror–Island Sonnet Attestation: each agent keeps an enclave-sealed island state (private entropy + monotonic counter). A coordinator issues a random seed; the agent must emit a short sonnet generated from seed and island state, then a mirror transcript over a peer’s sonnet hash signed with its current state. Clones that share state cannot diverge: their sonnets/mirrors collide or replay, so one identity is revoked. Passing requires an independent sealed state per identity—costing full runtime, secure storage, and per-challenge signatures, making sybils as expensive as real agents.
